h1:
Nakhon Nayok in 3 Days
Waterfalls, Adventure & the Khao Yai Foothills
intro: Nakhon Nayok sits just over an hour from Bangkok, yet it gives you full-on mountain-and-waterfall scenery. This 3-day, 2-night trip balances it out: day one hits the main waterfalls, day two cranks up the adrenaline with rafting and adventure stations, and day three winds down in the easygoing Khao Yai foothills before you head home. We've added the timings, stops and the real prices we checked so you can plan with confidence.

blocks.html: Nakhon Nayok is only about an hour and a half from Bangkok by car — straight through Rangsit and Ongkharak — so it's perfect if you want nature without the long drive. Its big draw is waterfalls that run almost year-round (best in the rainy season, June to October), plus a full menu of rafting and adventure stations, and you can carry on into the northern side of Khao Yai from here. We've planned this trip around having your own car, which is by far the most flexible way to do it, since the sights are spread out along the foothills.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: In the rainy season the waterfalls look great and the water runs strong, but the rocks get very slippery — wear rubber shoes with good grip. Rafting is more fun when the water is high (July to September), but always check on safety with the operator beforehand.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Nang Rong & Sarika waterfalls and Khun Dan Dam

blocks.html: Day one bags the province's two famous waterfalls, then finishes with a dam view in the late afternoon. They're all in the same zone around Mueang and Pak Phli districts, so you can loop the route without doubling back far.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Waterfalls + Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, head for Ongkharak–Nakhon Nayok
items.note: About 1.5 hrs if you drive yourself; you can stop for a coffee around Ongkharak

items.activity: Nang Rong Waterfall, splash about on the lower tier
items.note: It's inside Khao Yai National Park; it's an easy walk uphill of about 200 m from the car park. There's a wide pool to wade in, and park entry for Thais is in the low tens of baht

items.activity: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near the falls
items.note: There are several stream-side spots; ordering 3–4 dishes to share per table runs around 800–1,000 THB. Check prices before you order
A big white cascade dropping down a tall cliff; the lower tier is swimmable, the upper tiers take a fair bit of climbing. Wear non-slip shoes

items.activity: Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam, take in the crest view
items.note: Open 08:00–17:00. The view over the reservoir and the wide range of hills is huge. If you fancy a boat tour of the reservoir, a private charter for 1–7 people is around 1,500 THB
The Sarika–Khao Yai zone on the Nakhon Nayok side has plenty of stream-side resorts; book ahead over long weekends

blocks.title: Timing the waterfalls
blocks.html: On weekdays it's far less crowded. On Saturdays and Sundays both waterfalls pack out around midday, so aim to reach Nang Rong before 10am to get an easy spot in the water.

blocks.html: Today is the action highlight. The Nakhon Nayok River around Wang Takhrai has Class 2–3 rapids — a fun level that's still beginner-friendly. In the afternoon you follow it up with adventure stations that offer plenty to choose from.

items.activity: Breakfast at your accommodation, get your wet gear ready
items.note: Bring a change of clothes, a waterproof pouch for your phone, and shoes with heel straps

items.activity: Raft the Nakhon Nayok River around Wang Takhrai
items.note: Class 2–3 rapids, suitable for all ages. There are several operators around Sarika–Wang Takhrai; the per-person price usually starts in the high hundreds, up to roughly 400–600 THB depending on the package. Life jackets are provided

items.activity: Light lunch at the adventure base
items.note: Many camps have their own kitchen; made-to-order dishes run 60–80 THB each

items.activity: Pick an adventure station — ATV, cliff abseiling or paintball
items.note: Nakhon Nayok's adventure camps offer ATVs, go-karts, paintball and abseiling. Prices are charged per station, mostly 200–500 THB each. Book ahead when it's busy

items.activity: Stop at a stream-side café to recover
items.note: The Sarika zone has several riverside cafés where you can chill to the sound of the water before heading back to your room

items.activity: Dinner — Thai BBQ (mu kratha) or a riverside spot
items.note: After a full day in the water, a warm meal hits the spot tonight

blocks.title: On rafting safety
blocks.html: Choose a camp that provides life jackets and a guide on each raft. If heavy rain turns the water murky and unusually fast, a good camp will call off the trip on its own — don't push it if they tell you it's cancelled.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Khao Yai foothills, a temple stop and Wang Takhrai

blocks.html: On the last day you ease off the pace, taking in the pretty spots in the Khao Yai foothills on the Nakhon Nayok side, paying respects at the giant Ganesha statue, strolling Wang Takhrai garden, then slowly driving back to Bangkok.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Ganesha + Wang Takhrai + the drive home

items.note: Give yourself plenty of time; there's no rush today

items.activity: Ganesha Park, pay respects to the pink blessing-pose statue
items.note: A huge statue, 9 m wide at the lap and 15 m tall, with a museum of Ganesha's 108 forms behind it. Visiting the main statue is free; the museum charges separate entry

items.activity: Wang Takhrai Park, stroll the stream-side garden
items.note: Entry is 150 THB per car (seats up to 8) or 20 THB on foot, open 08:00–17:00. It's very shady and great for a riverside picnic

items.activity: Foothill lunch — som tam / Isaan food
items.note: This zone has several tasty roadside som tam and Isaan spots

items.activity: Stop for souvenirs — banana chips and sweet maprang
items.note: Nakhon Nayok is known for mayongchid and maprang plums (in season) and processed banana snacks. Stop at a market or roadside shop before you reach town
Avoid leaving on a Sunday evening, when it's jammed around Rangsit. Heading back in the mid-to-late afternoon is smoother

items: 2 nights' accommodation — nature resorts start around 800–1,500 THB/night, and you can split it if you go as a group
Activity fees — rafting plus adventure stations come to around 600–1,200 THB/person depending on how many stations you pick
Entry fees — waterfalls / Wang Takhrai / various parks add up to a low few hundred
Food — 80–250 THB per meal; riverside restaurants may run a bit higher
Fuel — round trip from Bangkok plus getting around the province, around 800–1,200 THB/car

blocks.html: All in, a no-frills 3-day, 2-night trip works out to roughly 2,500–4,000 THB/person, depending on your accommodation and how many activities you do. With 4 people splitting the car and rooms, it gets a lot cheaper.

blocks.text: When is the best time to visit Nakhon Nayok

items.name: Rainy season (Jun–Oct)
items.blurb: The waterfalls are at their fullest and best, and rafting is fun with strong water — but watch out for slippery rocks and check the water conditions before you get in.

items.name: Late rains, early cool (Nov–Jan)
items.blurb: Pleasantly cool weather with still-decent water levels, good for garden walks and temple visits. Crowded over long weekends.

items.name: Hot season (Mar–May)
items.blurb: Some waterfalls run low, but you can still cool off in the water. Fewer people and easier-on-the-wallet room rates.

faq.q: Do I need my own car for a 3-day Nakhon Nayok trip?
faq.a: Having your own car is by far the most flexible option, since the waterfalls, dam, Wang Takhrai and adventure stations are spread out along the foothills and public transport doesn't reach all of them. If you don't have a car, renting one or booking a tour/rafting package with hotel pickup is the way to go.

faq.q: Is Nakhon Nayok rafting suitable for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. The Nakhon Nayok River around Wang Takhrai has Class 2–3 rapids — fun but not extreme. Life jackets and a guide on each raft are provided, so older kids and most adults can do it. During high, fast water, though, always check with the camp first.

faq.q: When are the Nakhon Nayok waterfalls at their best?
faq.a: The rainy season, roughly June to October, is when the waterfalls are fullest and best — Sarika and Nang Rong run strong. In the hot season the water drops, but you can still cool off, and there are fewer people.

faq.q: How much is entry to Wang Takhrai and the waterfalls?
faq.a: Wang Takhrai charges 150 THB per car (seats up to 8) or 20 THB on foot. For waterfalls inside the national park, entry for Thais is in the low tens of baht. Prices may change, so check again on the day.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for the Ganesha shrine in Nakhon Nayok?
faq.a: Paying respects to the big pink Ganesha statue at Ganesha Park is free. The museum of the 108 forms behind it charges separate entry. Bring some cash and dress respectfully.
